title: The Cost of Music: Has Digitization Made Copyright Obsolete?
affiliations: Michigan State University - College of Law and University of Oregon School of Law

detail.title: The Cost of Music: Has Digitization Made Copyright Obsolete?

publicationDetails.detailsText: NYU Journal of Intellectual Property & Entertainment Law, Volume 15, No. 1, Pp. 225–329 (2025).

detail.abstract:
Commentators have repeatedly claimed that digital technologies render producers and recording engineers effectively obsolete. Supposedly, any DIY musician with a laptop and GarageBand can make home recordings that sound just as good as professionals in a high-end studio. The result is a dramatic reduction in the cost of music and the barriers to entry. As artists increasingly record and release new tracks entirely on their own, commentators hail the democratization of the music industry.

Copyright skeptics have invoked democratization claims to further their own agenda: They argue that because digital democratization has eviscerated music production costs, artists no longer need copyright protection to recoup their up-front investment. As such, sound recording copyrights may no longer be justified.

Our Article examines the reality underlying such democratization claims. Harnessing both quantitative and qualitative data, we shed empirical light on a debate hitherto fueled by theory and anecdotes. Our findings call into question the commercial viability of DIY music. We show that instances of genuine DIY music gaining widespread popularity remain rare—roughly 1% of music appearing in the top 200 weekly charts is self-produced by artists.

Our Article also provides a qualitative context to explain why DIY recordings have failed to gain traction on commercial charts. Drawing on extensive interviews with music industry insiders, we delve into the complexities of the music recording process and explore the hidden pitfalls that hold DIY artists back. Moreover, contrary to the claims of democratization evangelists, we show that the time and costs required to produce commercially competitive music have not have significantly changed in the digital age. Our findings strongly suggest that copyright skeptics have overstated their case: The rationale for the sound recording copyrights in the digital age remain fundamentally intact.

title: An Axiomatic, Mathematical Derivation of Interest Rate Dynamics using the Kolmogorov Forward Equation
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: An Axiomatic, Mathematical Derivation of Interest Rate Dynamics using the Kolmogorov Forward Equation
detail.abstract: This working paper develops an axiomatic framework for modelling the dynamics of the instantaneous rolling forward rate (IRFR) and, in turn, the entire term structure of interest rates. Unlike traditional term-structure models, which typically posit a stochastic process a priori, this framework derives the IRFR dynamics directly from four structural axioms that encode fundamental behavioural and probabilistic properties of interest rates. Together, these axioms may uniquely determine both the drift and diffusion components of the IRFR and imply that the forward-rate process must take the form of a Pearson diffusion with linear drift and quadratic volatility. The resulting diffusion structure arises endogenously and applies specifically to the IRFR rather than to the short rate or other macro-financial factors. The axioms generate several notable implications, including a structural relationship between the short-and long-maturity ends of the forward curve: at equilibrium, the instantaneous forward rate with zero time to maturity equals one half of the long-run asymptotic forward rate. This relationship does not arise in standard affine models and provides a new benchmark for evaluating monetary-policy neutrality. The axioms further imply that the full forward curve can be reconstructed from any single observed forward rate together with the long-run asymptotic level, with the curve's shape constrained to an exponential-decay structure. Deviations from this form-such as humps or twists-are interpreted as signatures of external policy intervention. Solving the Kolmogorov Forward Equation under the derived dynamics additionally shows that the stationary distribution of the IRFR is a shifted inverse-gamma distribution: a heavy-tailed, strictly positive law consistent with empirical interest-rate behaviour. Collectively, these results establish a unified, structurally derived foundation for IRFR dynamics that links equilibrium behaviour, forward-curve evolution, and long-run probabilistic structure.

detail.title: When Governors Flip, Boards Pause

detail.abstract: I study how public firms adjust visible governance turnover after close gubernatorial elections. The central fact is a mirror image. When a close election flips the governor's party, firms file fewer Item 5.02 disclosures reporting director and officer turnover. When an equally close election leaves party control in place, filings increase. Linking SEC filings, BoardEx, Compustat, and gubernatorial elections for 9,283 firms across 271 elections from 2004 to 2024, I show that broad regime change is a null, while close party flips reduce director and officer change filings by about 12% and equally close non-flips increase them by about 10%. In my primary close-only design, party change lowers filings by 14.6% of the close-election baseline. The decline appears after inauguration rather than immediately after election day. Annual board evidence shows what follows the pause: after close flips, boards expand and add politically connected directors. I interpret the evidence as a pause-and-rebuild response in which surprise regime turnover temporarily slows visible board reshuffling while firms adapt to a new political regime.

title: Covariate-Separated Hybrid Neural-Gaussian Process Modeling Of Equity Market Dynamics
affiliations: , Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi, Ghana., Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi, Ghana., Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi, Ghana., Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi, Ghana. and Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi, Ghana.

detail.title: Covariate-Separated Hybrid Neural-Gaussian Process Modeling Of Equity Market Dynamics
detail.abstract: Forecasting stock returns is challenging due to the nonlinear, nonstationary, and regime-dependent nature of financial markets. This study proposes a hybrid semiparametric model that integrates a feedforward neural network (FNN) and a Gaussian process (GP) to model return dynamics jointly. The approach is based on a principled covariate separation strategy, in which discrete regime-based variables are assigned to the neural network to capture nonlinear interactions, while continuous technical indicators are modeled using a Gaussian process to leverage its probabilistic structure and support uncertainty quantification. The model is estimated using a two-stage procedure in which the GP is fitted to the residuals of the neural network, allowing the two components to complement each other. Results using daily Apple Inc (AAPL) equity data indicate that the proposed hybrid model substantially improves predictive performance, achieving an R 2 of 0.757 and an RMSE of 0.00997 compared to standalone FNN and GP models, and also provides well-calibrated uncertainty estimates. These findings highlight the importance of aligning model structure with the statistical properties of financial predictors and contribute to the growing literature on hybrid machine learning approaches in financial econometrics.

title: Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Control of Traffic Networks with Contextual Information

detail.title: Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Control of Traffic Networks with Contextual Information

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there is no conflict of interest regarding the publication of this paper.

detail.abstract: Transportation networks are increasingly exposed to contextual disturbances such as weather events, traffic incidents, and demand surges. Existing traffic management pipelines typically adopt a decoupled predict-then-optimize architecture, where contextual information is first used to forecast network parameters and the resulting predictions are subsequently incorporated into optimization models. While computationally convenient, this separation fails to integrate contextual signals directly into the continuous-time dynamics governing traffic flow. This paper develops a continuous-time optimal control framework in which contextual information dynamically modifies the congestion structure of the transportation network. Contextual variables are modeled as bounded signals that deform the network's macroscopic capacity landscape. Within this formulation, the traffic management problem is characterized by a contextual Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation that yields an optimal feedback policy mapping traffic states and contextual observations directly to operational control actions. We establish theoretical guarantees showing that the HJB value function acts as a control Lyapunov function for the closed-loop network dynamics. Under bounded contextual disturbances, the resulting policy guarantees bounded queue growth and asymptotic throughput recovery. To address the computational challenges of solving high-dimensional HJB equations, the value function is approximated using physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). Numerical experiments on a two-region urban network governed by macroscopic fundamental diagrams demonstrate that the contextual HJB controller mitigates congestion amplification and restores network throughput more rapidly than reactive control and predict-then-optimize baselines.

title: Validating Large Language Model Annotations

detail.title: Validating Large Language Model Annotations
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a validation framework for LLM-generated measurements when reliable benchmarks are unavailable. Validity is established by testing whether an LLM can reconstruct passages from annotated labels while maintaining semantic consistency with the original text. The framework avoids circular reasoning by establishing testable prerequisite properties that must be met for a validation to be considered successful. Application to news article data demonstrates that the framework serves as a practical alternative to human benchmarking, which offers advantages in objectivity, scalability, and cost-effectiveness while identifying cases where LLMs capture economic meaning that human evaluators miss.

detail.title: Salience and (Non-)Buyer's Remorse: Optimal Nonlinear Pricing with Cognitively Constrained Consumers

publicationDetails.detailsText: University of Chicago, Becker Friedman Institute for Economics Working Paper No. 2026-52
publicationDetails.journalName: Becker Friedman Institute for Economics Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Nonlinear pricing theory predicts that firms can extract surplus by inducing heterogeneous consumers to self-sort across price contract offers that are ex-post optimal for them. We study subscription pricing when the frictionless sorting assumption fails. Using large-scale subscription experiments conducted by Lyft, we document systematic deviations from optimal self-selection: many high-demand consumers decline subscriptions that would have saved them money, while some subscribers fail to break even. We develop a structural model of intensive-margin demand in which consumers may exhibit salience failures, forecast errors about future demand, or impulsivity. We show that subscription uptake can be recast as one-sided noncompliance in a binary-instrument framework, allowing us to leverage LATE methods to identify counterfactual outcome distributions and a novel "uptake function" linking baseline outcomes to compliance behavior. Combining experimental price variation with this identification strategy, we recover utility primitives, demand heterogeneity, and behavioral parameters. Salience failures and forecast errors play quantitatively important roles. Counterfactual analyses show that optimal subscription pricing generates substantial gains relative to linear pricing, but these gains are highly sensitive to consumer deviations from ex-post optimal choice. Implementing nonlinear pricing therefore requires not only optimal contract design for consumer screening, but also coordinated efforts to mitigate behavioral frictions.

detail.title: Complexity Breaks Arbitrage Pricing Theory

publicationDetails.detailsText: Fisher College of Business Working Paper No. 2026-03-005
publicationDetails.journalName: Ohio State University, Fisher College of Business Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Arbitrage Pricing Theory predicts pricing errors vanish as markets grow. Three findings reverse this prediction. First, under estimation uncertainty, equilibrium pricing errors scale as N/t (number of assets over sample size), with a persistent component from time-varying fundamentals that no estimator can eliminate. Second, the stochastic discount factor loads primarily on estimation errors rather than fundamental risk factors, explaining why risk-based factor models fail to price assets. Third, multiple strategies achieve high Sharpe ratios with low cross-correlations as they exploit distinct dimensions of the growing estimation error space. When investors disagree about expected returns, mispricing persists even with informed investors because risk aversion prevents them from taking sufficiently large positions to eliminate complexity-driven pricing errors. Empirically, individual stock returns require 145 principal components to explain half their variance. Systematic hedge funds’ active positions exhibit near-zero correlations (average 0.07), consistent with exploitation of distinct estimation-error dimensions.

detail.abstract: This study examines the relationship between CPI inflation and stock market performance in India, focusing on the NIFTY 50 during the period 2015–2023. The analysis incorporates the structural break caused by the COVID-19 (2020– 2021) to assess whether inflation significantly influences daily stock returns and volatility. Using time-series econometric techniques, including Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression, Granger causality testing, and a GARCH (1,1) model, the study evaluates both mean return effects and volatility persistence. The results indicate that CPI inflation does not have a statistically significant impact on daily NIFTY 50 returns, nor does it Granger-cause stock performance. However, volatility increased substantially during the COVID-19 period, and GARCH estimates confirm strong volatility clustering and persistence. The findings suggest that inflation affects market risk more than average returns, particularly during periods of macroeconomic uncertainty. These insights are relevant for investors and policymakers in understanding how macroeconomic shocks transmit into financial markets.

title: rmsBMA: Reduced Model Space Bayesian Model Averaging
affiliations: Lazarski University

detail.title: rmsBMA: Reduced Model Space Bayesian Model Averaging

declarations.funderStatement: This article was prepared within the research project “Bayesian simultaneous equations model averaging - theoretical development and R package,” funded by the Polish National Science Centre, on the basis of the decision No. DEC-2021/43/B/HS4/01745.

detail.abstract: This article introduces the rmsBMA R package for Bayesian model averaging in settings with many candidate regressors relative to the available sample size. The package implements reduced model space BMA by restricting attention to models with at most M regressors. This restriction preserves degrees of freedom for estimation and inference and concentrates posterior mass on parsimonious specifications, while still accounting for model uncertainty within the admissible subset of models. rmsBMA supports standard prior structures used in the BMA literature, including Zellner-type g-priors and alternative model priors with appropriate truncation under model space reduction. The package further provides heteroscedasticity-consistent inference, Extreme Bounds Analysis, jointness measures, and graphical tools for exploring prior and posterior model probabilities, model size distributions, and coefficient distributions. In addition, it introduces group dilution, a non-empirical rule that penalizes models containing multiple proxies for the same theoretical construct. An empirical application illustrates the workflow.

title: Human-Centered Innovation: A Multiplicative Theory of Value and Adoption Using the ABC × β-Vector Model
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Human-Centered Innovation: A Multiplicative Theory of Value and Adoption Using the ABC × β-Vector Model
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the ABC × β-vector framework, a multiplicative theory of human-centered value and adoption. It proposes that value exists only when three dimensions coexist: Appeal (emotional and cultural resonance), Benefits (functional effectiveness), and Convenience (practical ease), such that A × B × C > 0. A value maturity vector (β_A, β_B,β_C) explains why different adopter segments require different levels of maturity in each dimension, and reframes Moore’s “chasm” as a contextually determined step-change in Convenience maturity rather than a psychological barrier. The framework is illustrated through nine case studies — iPhone, Airbnb, Uber, Tesla, Android, Ford Model T, Google Glass, Segway, and Webvan — demonstrating both explanatory and predictive power across breakthrough successes, strategic niche plays, and canonical failures. β-values are presented as strategic estimation anchors pending empirical validation. The paper builds on the author’s Human-Centered Organizations framework (Tawakkol, 2025).

title: A Strategic Pure Exchange Game with Single-Peaked Preferences: A Generalization of the Garbage Disposal Game
affiliations: Nagoya-Gakuin University

detail.title: A Strategic Pure Exchange Game with Single-Peaked Preferences: A Generalization of the Garbage Disposal Game
detail.abstract: This paper studies a strategic pure exchange game with single-peaked preferences in which each player's peak for each commodity lies below the initial endowment. Extending the garbage disposal game of Hirai, Masuzawa, and Nakayama (2006), we allow the status of a commodity as a good or a bad to depend on the final allocation. We examine four solution concepts: strong Nash equilibrium, coalition-proof Nash equilibrium, α-stability, and β-stability. In the one-commodity case, we show that a natural analogue of a strategy profile introduced in the garbage disposal game is a strong Nash equilibrium. We also provide two sufficient conditions for the existence of coalition-proof Nash equilibrium, show that continuity of utility functions guarantees β-stability and hence α-stability, and show by example that α-stability does not imply β-stability.

title: Modeling Heterogeneity in the Commitment-Engagement Link: A Bayesian Approach Integrating Textual Evaluations of Experiential Attributes
affiliations: Meiji University and Meiji University

detail.title: Modeling Heterogeneity in the Commitment-Engagement Link: A Bayesian Approach Integrating Textual Evaluations of Experiential Attributes
detail.abstract: This study proposes a Bayesian hierarchical model to investigate the heterogeneity in the relationship between customer commitment and engagement by integrating construct measurements and textual customer reviews. While traditional models often assume a uniform impact of commitment on engagement, our approach incorporates textual customer experience evaluations to capture diverse response patterns in behavioral engagement. The empirical analysis reveals significant individual differences in how affective and continuance commitment relate to engagement outcomes. The results indicate that the impact of these two commitment dimensions may vary based on the particular experiential attributes. In several cases, either the affective or the continuance psychological pathway appears to be more prominent in driving engagement. Although these results should be interpreted with caution because of the multicollinearity inherent in the measurement scales, this study provides a granular framework for managers to strategically tailor experiential attributes to activate specific commitment drivers. The proposed method contributes to a deeper understanding of the psychological mechanisms that drive customer engagement.

title: Recession as Forcing Function: Permanent Displacement in AI-Exposed Occupations
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Recession as Forcing Function: Permanent Displacement in AI-Exposed Occupations
detail.abstract: Despite rapid advances in AI capability, labor market displacement has remained largely deferred. The gap between what AI systems can theoretically perform and what they are observed performing in enterprise workflows remains substantial, and employment in exposed occupations has not declined meaningfully. This paper argues that deferral is a function of economic stability-a condition that recessions rupture. Drawing on Massenkoff & McCrory's (2026) observed exposure framework and the historical automation literature, this paper introduces the recession-AI interaction hypothesis: that a significant economic recession will serve as a forcing function for AI adoption in enterprise, compressing years of gradual adoption into a single downturn cycle and producing employment levels in exposed occupations that do not recover to pre-recession baselines. The mechanism operates through three reinforcing channels: cost pressure driving adoption threshold crossings, institutional lock-in preventing reversion, and continuous AI capability improvement raising the productivity floor during and after the contraction. Unlike prior recession-driven automation cycles, the technology available at the moment of adoption does not remain static-it advances, permanently weakening the economic rationale for restoring prior staffing models. The implications are asymmetric across occupation and seniority, with entry-level knowledge workers facing the most immediate exposure and the experience accumulation pipeline that produces senior talent facing structural compression.

title: Dual-Ledger Architecture for Auditable Hypothesis Tracking: Separating Facts from Interpretations in Intelligence Analysis

detail.title: Dual-Ledger Architecture for Auditable Hypothesis Tracking: Separating Facts from Interpretations in Intelligence Analysis

detail.abstract: Intelligence analysis, risk assessment, and forecasting systems face a persistent problem: confirmation bias and echo chambers emerge when analysts interpret ambiguous evidence through pre-existing beliefs. Existing approaches-large language models, Bayesian updating, and manual structured analytic techniques-fail to provide systematic protection against these cognitive pitfalls while maintaining auditability and temporal integrity in high-accountability, long-horizon reasoning contexts such as strategic intelligence assessment, policy evaluation, and regulated clinical or financial environments. This paper does not address real-time or high-throughput decision environments, where different architectural trade-offs apply. We propose a policy-parameterized deterministic approach for auditable hypothesis tracking and confidence updates under uncertainty, motivated by the broader problem of epistemic accountability in institutional reasoning. The approach is structured around three architectural elements: (1) a dual-ledger architecture that separates immutable world-layer facts from model-layer interpretations; (2) confidence propagation with anti-cascade damping and tunneling penalties intended to mitigate echo-chamber dynamics; and (3) mandatory review gates that require explicit human judgment at key confidence and conflict thresholds. The approach is illustrated via a prototype implementation and synthetic case studies. The proposed architecture uses only deterministic rules within a versioned policy regime (no machine learning and no LLM-based reasoning), prioritizing auditability and reproducibility. We describe the technical design, demonstrate operation through case studies, and report quantitative metrics. For instance, in Case 1 (opaque information ecosystem), four apparently independent sources with hidden shared influence yield a materially higher naive confidence under an independence assumption, but a lower final confidence after influence-aware discounting, reducing overconfidence under correlated evidence.

title: Content Platform GenAI Regulation via Compensation
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)

detail.title: Content Platform GenAI Regulation via Compensation
detail.abstract: The use of Generative AI (GenAI) for creative content generation has gained popularity in recent years. GenAI allows creators to generate contents that are increasingly becoming indistinguishable to the human-generated counterpart at a much lower cost. While GenAI reshapes the competitive landscape of the contents market, the original creators were typically not compensated for their works that were used in the GenAI training. On the other hands, the widespread adoption of GenAI threatens to replace the humangenerated shares of contents on content platforms, contaminating training data source for future GenAI models. In this paper, we argue that an unregulated usage of GenAI can also be harmful to the platform by causing a contents distribution distortion which can lower the consumers' engagement and the platform's profit. We show that a simple economically-driven creator compensation scheme, can incentivize more creation of highvalue human-generated contents, without the need for an AI-detector. This reduces the data pollution for future GenAI training, while improves the consumer engagement and the platform's profit.

Credance and the Islamic Repo 
Why the Real Work is Epistemic, Not Legal

detail.abstract: This paper introduces the concept of credance-the collective belief that makes a financial market possible before any track record exists-and applies it to the development of the Islamic repo market. Distinct from credibility, which is attributed after the fact on the basis of demonstrated performance, credance is anterior: it is the shared epistemic condition that enables the first transaction. Drawing on the historical precedent of the eurodollar market (London, 1955-1963) and on Searle's (1995) theory of social reality construction, we argue that market infrastructure does not produce credance; credance produces market infrastructure. This sequencing has been systematically misread in analyses of Islamic repo development, including in the context of the IIFM/ICMA Iʿaadat Al Shiraʿa Master Agreement. We further argue that Islamic finance is epistemic by essence-the technical submits to meaning-and that the MENA/Southeast Asia fracture in Islamic repo credance reflects divergent interpretations of Quranic financial language across different legal traditions rather than a regulatory or infrastructure deficit. The paper concludes with implications for sequencing Islamic repo market development and with a policy recommendation for multilateral institutions: the financing of scholarly dialogue and interpretive convergence is a precondition for market development, not a luxury that follows it.

detail.abstract: The metaverse, driven by advances in augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and artificial intelligence (AI), is reshaping digital marketing while raising complex ethical challenges. This systematic literature review analyzes fifty peer-reviewed literature reviews (2019-2024) retrieved from Scopus and AISeL, focusing on digital marketing, branding, and the metaverse. The review maps objectives, themes, contribution types, publication outlets, and methodologies, showing that most contributions are theoretical (68%), followed by empirical (16%), methodological (12%), and opinionbased (4%), with PRISMA emerging as the dominant reporting standard. Through meta-synthesis, we identify and analyze four core ethical dimensions: privacy, transparency, authenticity, and fairness. By integrating insights across fragmented domains, the review highlights how these ethical challenges intersect and require interdisciplinary responses involving marketers, platform providers, policymakers, and consumers. We advance theoretical implications by linking immersive marketing to foundational perspectives such as privacy theory, media richness, self-determination, and algorithmic transparency, while also outlining nine actionable implications for practice and future research. In doing so, this review of reviews establishes a foundation for responsible, inclusive, and sustainable digital marketing in the metaverse.

detail.title: Human-AI Collaboration in Radiology: The Case of Pulmonary Embolism

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflicts of interest.

detail.abstract: We study how radiologists use AI to diagnose pulmonary embolism (PE), the third leading cause of cardiovascular death in the U.S. We track over 100,000 scans interpreted by nearly 400 radiologists during the staggered rollout of an FDA-approved diagnostic platform in a large hospital system. When AI flags PE, radiologists agree 84% of the time; when AI predicts no PE, they agree 97%. Disagreement evolves substantially: radiologists initially reject AI-positive PEs in 30% of cases, dropping to 12% by year two. Despite a 16% increase in scan volume, diagnostic speed remains stable while per-radiologist monthly volumes nearly double. We document substantial heterogeneity in AI collaboration: some radiologists reject AI-flagged PEs half the time while others accept nearly always; female radiologists are 6 percentage points less likely to override AI than male radiologists. Moderate AI engagement correlates with highest agreement, whereas both low and high engagement show more disagreement. Follow-up imaging reveals that when radiologists override AI to diagnose PE, 54% of subsequent scans show both agreeing on no PE within 30 days. Patient outcomes differ systematically by agreement category. When both AI and radiologist agree on PE presence, 30-day mortality increases 3.4 percentage points relative to concordant negatives. When only the radiologist diagnoses PE, mortality increases 5.5 percentage points. When only the AI detects PE but the radiologist does not, mortality increases 4.0 percentage points. Radiologist overrides to diagnose PE correlate with higher rates of right heart failure and respiratory failure than AI positives rejected by radiologists. These patterns may reflect radiologists identifying clinically significant cases that AI misses, radiologist diagnoses triggering more aggressive treatment, or diagnostic errors where radiologists see PE in sicker patients who lack it. The modest mortality differences across disagreement categories suggest patient severity matters more than who detects the PE.

title: Local Embeddedness and Subsidiary Autonomy in MNC Knowledge Transfer: A Comparison of R&D and Marketing Functions

detail.title: Local Embeddedness and Subsidiary Autonomy in MNC Knowledge Transfer: A Comparison of R&D and Marketing Functions
detail.abstract: This study examines how local embeddedness and subsidiary autonomy differ between R&D and marketing functions in multinational company (MNC) subsidiaries, and what these differences imply for knowledge transfer configurations. Drawing on survey data from 558 employees across 26 MNC subsidiaries in the ICT and automotive industries, combined with qualitative interviews from 35 managers, we find significant functional differences in subsidiary-headquarters relationships. R&D functions exhibit higher information dependence on headquarters, greater geographic proximity to local technical networks, and more frequent knowledge sharing through international working groups and assignments. In contrast, marketing functions demonstrate higher reliance on expatriates for knowledge transfer and greater autonomy over local marketing strategies. Notably, we identify two distinct dimensions of subsidiary autonomy: while marketing functions enjoy greater autonomy over local strategies, R&D functions possess greater autonomy over human resources (HR) and financial decisions. These findings challenge the implicit assumption in prior research that subsidiaries can be treated as homogeneous units and reveal a sophisticated 'give-and-take' governance mechanism whereby MNCs balance control and autonomy differently across functional domains.​

title: AI and the Acceleration of Responsibility in Sociotechnical Organizations

detail.title: AI and the Acceleration of Responsibility in Sociotechnical Organizations
detail.abstract: Responsibility in regulated organizations does not emerge only after failure; it is continuously produced through anticipatory alignment, procedural embedding, and retrospective stabilization. As artificial intelligence (AI) systems become integrated into documentation and evaluative infrastructures, responsibility is increasingly mediated through computational representation. Yet AI does not introduce new accountability structures. Instead, it reshapes the temporal dynamics through which responsibility becomes stabilized. This paper introduces Premature Accountability Convergence (PAC), a conditional acceleration dynamic within the responsibility lifecycle. PAC occurs when computational mediation compresses interpretive space such that responsibility stabilizes before causal ambiguity has been meaningfully examined. Under conditions of representational compression, epistemic authority amplification, and temporal contraction of sensemaking, responsibility may converge while plausible alternative explanations remain insufficiently explored. By conceptualizing AI as a representational accelerator rather than an autonomous decision-maker, this framework shifts attention from algorithmic bias toward the temporal architecture of accountability. PAC extends sociotechnical theories of responsibility by specifying how computational infrastructures intensify stabilization dynamics already embedded within organizational systems. Rather than determining who is responsible, AI may reshape how quickly and how narrowly responsibility becomes administratively actionable.

title: Responsibility Convergence in Organizational Investigations: Structural Dynamics of Blame in Root Cause Analysis

detail.title: Responsibility Convergence in Organizational Investigations: Structural Dynamics of Blame in Root Cause Analysis
detail.abstract: Organizational investigations such as root cause analysis (RCA) are intended to identify systemic causes of failure and support organizational learning. Yet across regulated and safety-critical environments, investigative conclusions recurrently stabilize responsibility at identifiable individuals despite formal commitments to system-oriented explanation. This persistent actor-centered pattern presents a theoretical puzzle: why do investigative systems designed to diffuse responsibility across sociotechnical structures so often concentrate accountability at particular organizational members? This paper develops a structural explanation for this recurrent stabilization dynamic, termed responsibility convergence. Responsibility convergence refers to the patterned concentration of accountability at identifiable actors when investigative processes translate causal ambiguity into administratively actionable conclusions. The framework specifies how convergence arises from the interaction of three mechanisms: procedural ambiguity, attributional closure pressure, and accountability legibility bias. Under conditions of underdetermined causal reconstruction, organizations face institutional pressure to stabilize responsibility assignments. Identifiable individuals constitute the most interpretable and administratively actionable attribution anchors within accountability infrastructures. As a result, attribution systematically concentrates on actors rather than distributed structural conditions. By situating investigative convergence within broader organizational responsibility alignment dynamics, the paper clarifies why system-oriented investigative frameworks recurrently produce actor-centered accountability outcomes. The analysis develops a mechanism-based account of convergence, derives theoretical propositions, and outlines implications for organizational learning and accountability system design.

title: Anticipated Accountability Convergence: How Organizational Infrastructures Align Interpretations of Defensible Action

detail.title: Anticipated Accountability Convergence: How Organizational Infrastructures Align Interpretations of Defensible Action
detail.abstract: In regulated organizational environments, actors routinely orient their actions toward anticipated future evaluation, calibrating conduct under conditions in which decisions must later be auditable, traceable, and defensible. Prior research has largely examined accountability retrospectively, focusing on blame attribution, causal reasoning, and legitimacy repair after outcomes occur (Heider, 1958; Weiner, 1985; Hood, 2011). This retrospective emphasis obscures a structurally prior dimension of regulated work: accountability also operates as a prospective structuring condition shaping the interpretive field within which action unfolds. This paper introduces anticipated accountability convergence (AAC), a process-level framework explaining how organizational systems align expectations of accountable action before execution occurs. Rather than a psychological account of individual anticipation, AAC theorizes a structural alignment process through which accountability expectations become mutually reinforcing across procedural rules, documentation regimes, and evaluative architectures. The unit of analysis is therefore not individual accountability perception but the organizational infrastructures that preconfigure what will count as defensible interpretation before action takes place. The paper further introduces the concept of calibrated convergence, arguing that the relationship between convergence intensity and organizational effectiveness follows a curvilinear pattern. While insufficient convergence generates interpretive fragmentation, excessive convergence produces rigidity that constrains adaptive responsiveness. In highly regulated settings, recalibration typically occurs not through voluntary organizational adjustment but through reactive mechanisms triggered by incident-driven shocks or accumulated operational deviations. Finally, the paper situates AAC within a broader responsibility lifecycle through which accountability expectations are prospectively structured, retrospectively stabilized, and recursively institutionalized in regulated sociotechnical systems. The framework offers implications for organizational control, procedural design, and the governance of AI-mediated accountability infrastructures.

title: Blurring the Lines: How Social Media Travel Influencers Navigate Organic and Sponsored Content

detail.title: Blurring the Lines: How Social Media Travel Influencers Navigate Organic and Sponsored Content
detail.abstract: This research seeks to examine the strategies employed by social media travel influencers (SMTIs) in managing their organic and sponsored posts, as well as their interactions with followers. This qualitative study utilized in-depth interviews with 24 SMTIs who possess a significant presence on social media platforms. The findings indicate that followers exhibit a preference for organic content. The strategies employed in sponsored content by influencers encompass the timing of posts, the number of product images, tie-in strategies, the creation of valuable and engaging content, and the use of implicit advertising language. The way SMTIs disclose sponsorships is perceived negatively by followers. This study highlights the tension between authenticity and commercial interest, offering insights for both academics and practitioners in digital marketing and tourism promotion.

detail.abstract: An Exploration into the Journey of Community researches the essential role that community offers for individual identity, resilience, and existential becoming. Through an abductive, exploratory lens, this study interrogates the profound and often invisible mechanisms that generate enduring communal bonds, particularly in an era characterized by unprecedented forces of personal distraction, systemic polarization, digital mediation, and psychological isolation. This inquiry explores the intrinsic and emergent motivations that compel individuals to not merely seek community, but to engage in recursive patterns of deepening connection. Further, this paper examines how communal experiences reshape personal development within and beyond immediate social boundaries, while illuminating the complex phenomenological cycles of return that sustain meaningful, transformative human connections.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Banco de Espana Working Paper No. 2608
publicationDetails.journalName: Banco de Espana Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We use CPI micro data for nine euro area countries to document new evidence on consumer price stickiness in the euro area during the 2021-2024 inflation cycle. In 2022, the monthly frequency of price changes reached 12%, compared with an average of 8% over 2010–2019, roughly a four percentage point increase; it then fell quickly in 2023 and more slowly in 2024, ending close to its pre-pandemic level. The decline in the frequency of price changes was faster for food and non-energy industrial goods (NEIG) than for services, where frequencies remained elevated in 2024. The overall frequency rose mainly because there were more price increases, while the magnitude of the average size of the price increases or decreases changed only marginally during the surge. Products with a larger imported-energy cost share responded more strongly, and hazard-rate evidence shows that the probability of price adjustments increases with the gap between actual and optimal prices, consistent with state-dependent pricing and a steepening of the Phillips curve. To illustrate the implications of this state dependence, a macro model suggests that peak inflation would have been almost one percentage point lower had the frequency not responded to the inflation surge.

title: Coffee, Value Chains, and Commercial Diplomacy: Strengthening U.S.-Africa Trade Through Strategic Agricultural Partnerships

detail.title: Coffee, Value Chains, and Commercial Diplomacy: Strengthening U.S.-Africa Trade Through Strategic Agricultural Partnerships
detail.abstract:
Coffee remains one of the most important agricultural commodities linking African economies to global markets. Several African countries-including Ethiopia, Uganda, Kenya, Rwanda, and Tanzania-are among the world's leading coffee producers, while the United States is the largest coffee-consuming market. These structural dynamics create a natural foundation for deeper trade and investment partnerships between African coffee exporters and American buyers, roasters, and investors. Yet despite Africa's importance as a coffee-producing region, the continent captures only a small share of the value generated within global coffee markets. Most African countries continue to export unprocessed green coffee beans, while higher-value activities such as roasting, branding, and retail distribution remain concentrated in consumer markets. 

This paper examines the role of coffee value chains in shaping U.S.-Africa trade relations and explores how commercial diplomacy can strengthen agricultural partnerships between African producers and American markets. Drawing on data from the International Coffee Organization (ICO), the World Bank, the International Trade Centre (ITC), the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), and other global trade databases, the analysis investigates the structural dynamics of the global coffee industry and identifies key barriers that limit value capture for African producers. 

The paper further analyzes how trade promotion agencies, diplomatic missions, specialty coffee associations, and development institutions influence the evolution of U.S.-Africa coffee trade partnerships. Through comparative case studies of leading African coffee-producing countries including Uganda, Ethiopia, Kenya, and Rwanda—the paper evaluates strategies to expand value addition, improve market access, and strengthen investment linkages across the coffee value chain.

The findings suggest that deeper U.S.–Africa coffee partnerships could generate significant economic benefits for both sides. For African economies, expanding participation in higher-value segments of the coffee industry offers opportunities for rural development, export diversification, and industrial upgrading. For the United States, strengthening partnerships with African coffee producers supports supply chain diversification while contributing to the continued growth of the U.S. specialty coffee industry.

The paper concludes with policy recommendations aimed at strengthening agricultural trade diplomacy and promoting more equitable participation of African producers in global coffee value chains.

title: Bridging the Execution Gap: A Practitioner's Appraisal of PPP Governance for Bangladesh's Vision 2041

detail.title: Bridging the Execution Gap: A Practitioner's Appraisal of PPP Governance for Bangladesh's Vision 2041
detail.abstract: Bangladesh's journey toward Vision 2041 necessitates a transformative approach to infrastructure financing. With an annual investment gap exceeding USD 10 billion, Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) have become a strategic imperative. This paper evaluates current project appraisal frameworks in Bangladesh, contrasting them with global benchmarks from Australia, India, and the UK. By synthesizing document analysis with practitioner insights from the Planning Commission and the Bangladesh Economic Zones Authority (BEZA), the study identifies institutional bottlenecks and bankability gaps. It moves beyond theoretical discourse to address field-level challenges in risk allocation and procurement. The paper concludes with a roadmap for reform, emphasizing standardized Value for Money (VfM) assessments and the integration of SDG-linked sustainability safeguards to attract international capital.

title: Documenting Judgment: Cognitive Friction and Responsibility in Procedural Documentation

detail.title: Documenting Judgment: Cognitive Friction and Responsibility in Procedural Documentation
detail.abstract: Procedural documents such as Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) organize action and accountability in regulated work. While prior research has examined how responsibility is anticipated or stabilized through social and evaluative processes, procedural documents have often been treated primarily as coordination or standardization devices. Less attention has been paid to how procedural language itself structures the localized judgment demands that actors must resolve during execution. Drawing on a corpus of 500 procedurally realistic sentences derived from publicly available regulatory and safety documentation, including laboratory guidance, biosafety protocols, and chemical safety procedures, the analysis operationalizes cognitive friction as the cooccurrence of four structural features in procedural sentences: conditional branching, crossreferences, exception structures, and discretionary qualifiers. Rule-based computational annotation was used to identify feature distributions and co-occurrence patterns across the corpus. The results show that individual friction features are common across procedural genres, but structurally compounded judgment demands are concentrated within a smaller subset of sentences where conditional structures co-occur with referential or discretionary cues. These highfriction configurations concentrate interpretive resolution within localized procedural units while maintaining prescriptive accountability for execution. Across procedural sources, non-zero cognitive friction appears consistently, indicating that structurally embedded judgment demands are a general property of procedural text architecture rather than an artifact of any single institutional genre. By demonstrating that responsibility-relevant judgment demands can be operationalized at the level of procedural sentence structure, this study conceptualizes cognitive friction as a document-level mechanism and provides initial empirical evidence that such judgment demands are systematically embedded in procedural text architecture. This paper presents an initial empirical demonstration and is intended as a pilot study within a broader research program on responsibility in regulated sociotechnical systems.

title: Economic Diplomacy and the Strategic Role of African Embassies in Shaping U.S.-Africa Trade and Investment Partnerships

detail.title: Economic Diplomacy and the Strategic Role of African Embassies in Shaping U.S.-Africa Trade and Investment Partnerships
detail.abstract:
Economic diplomacy has become an increasingly important instrument of international engagement in a global economy characterized by expanding trade networks, rising investment flows, and intensifying competition for economic partnerships. As governments seek to advance national development objectives and strengthen participation in global markets, diplomatic institutions are playing an increasingly important role in facilitating commercial engagement between countries.

This paper examined the evolving role of African embassies in Washington, D.C. in advancing trade and investment partnerships between African economies and the United States. Drawing on literature in economic diplomacy, international political economy, and development policy, the study highlighted how diplomatic missions contribute to economic cooperation through activities such as export promotion, investment facilitation, diaspora engagement, and institutional partnership-building. These functions position embassies as key intermediaries that connect governments, private sector actors, development finance institutions, and research organizations across regions.

The analysis also explored several sectors that offer strong opportunities for expanding U.S.–Africa economic engagement, including agriculture and coffee value chains, digital innovation ecosystems, infrastructure development, and manufacturing. In addition, the paper examined broader structural trends shaping the future of economic cooperation, including the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area, Africa’s rapidly expanding consumer markets, and growing global demand for critical minerals required for the energy transition.

At the same time, the study highlighted the increasing importance of strengthening institutional capacity within diplomatic missions to support more effective economic diplomacy. Investments in commercial diplomacy training, improved coordination between embassies and domestic economic institutions, and expanded partnerships with diaspora networks and U.S. institutions can significantly enhance the effectiveness of embassy-based economic engagement strategies.

As Africa’s economic importance continues to grow in the coming decades, diplomatic missions will play an increasingly strategic role in shaping international economic cooperation with the continent. Strengthening embassy-based economic diplomacy frameworks can expand trade partnerships, attract investment, and support sustainable economic development across African economies while advancing the United States' economic interests.

title: AGOA, AfCTA, and the Future of U.S.-Africa Economic Relations: Policy Choices for a New Era of Trade Integration

detail.title: AGOA, AfCTA, and the Future of U.S.-Africa Economic Relations: Policy Choices for a New Era of Trade Integration
detail.abstract:
The evolution of economic relations between the United States and African economies has entered a critical transition period. The African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), enacted in 2000, has served as the cornerstone of U.S.–Africa trade policy for more than two decades, providing preferential access to the U.S. market for qualifying African countries. At the same time, Africa itself is undergoing a profound transformation through the creation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which seeks to establish a single integrated market across the continent. 

This paper examines the evolution of U.S.–Africa trade policy, evaluates the successes and limitations of AGOA, and analyzes the implications of AfCFTA for future trade integration between the United States and African economies. Drawing upon data from institutions including the United States International Trade Commission (USITC), the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), and the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), the paper assesses how U.S. trade policy has interacted with Africa’s evolving regional integration agenda.

The findings suggest that while AGOA has played a valuable role in expanding export opportunities for certain African economies, its long-term effectiveness is limited by structural features that do not fully align with Africa’s emerging continental trade architecture. As AfCFTA advances, U.S. trade policy must adapt to support deeper integration with regional markets and value chains. Strengthening economic partnerships with Africa offers significant benefits for the United States, including supply chain diversification, access to emerging markets, and strategic engagement with a region projected to represent a quarter of the global population by 2050.

title: Reducing Correspondent Banking Capital Requirements - Through Multilateral Netting with Threshold-Triggered Settlement

detail.title: Reducing Correspondent Banking Capital Requirements - Through Multilateral Netting with Threshold-Triggered Settlement
detail.abstract: The correspondent banking model remains expensive because banks must keep bilateral Nostro/Vostro balances pre-funded across the corridors they serve. That requirement ties up capital even before a payment is sent. This paper argues that the problem is not primarily a messaging problem; it is a settlement-capacity problem. It proposes a multilateral coordination mechanism built around three linked elements: real-time multilateral netting, threshold-triggered rolling settlement, and legally enforceable dispatch rights over members' existing custodial assets. In this structure, payment capacity comes from assets the bank already holds, rather than from new capital posted into a common pool. A Monte Carlo model calibrated to public BIS, McKinsey, and Basel documentation suggests that, under realistic corridor asymmetry, a 15-bank consortium could achieve netting compression in the 60-80% range. On those assumptions, annual capital-cost savings are estimated at roughly USD 150-400 million. The paper also sets out a staged default workflow-warning, throttle, suspension, self-cure, and forced dispatch-and identifies the main constraints that would determine whether the mechanism could move from theory to institutional use: settlement finality, RTGS reconciliation, legal enforceability across jurisdictions, per-currency capacity management, and regulatory classification.

detail.title: Driving Innovation through Content Marketing in Business Landscape: A Bibliometric Analysis of Global Research and Strategic Clusters
detail.abstract: This research aims to explore and evaluate the academic literature surrounding content marketing, employing bibliometric analysis to figure out the principal themes, authors, sources, highly cited works, leading countries, the most impactful keywords, and thematic content. A comprehensive bibliometric analysis was conducted on 490 publications from the Scopus Database spanning from 2008 to 2024, encompassing a range of formats such as published articles, conference papers, and book chapters. This paper presents the research findings, offering a comprehensive overview of insights and trends in the content marketing research domain. It includes patterns of scientific publications, important contributors such as authors and countries, sources, and the most cited and co-cited papers to uncover seminal publications and foundational knowledge. The co-occurrence keyword and bibliographic coupling analyses were employed to delineate intellectual networks and identify novel themes. A focused content analysis was conducted on 42 recent articles selected for their significance, accuracy, and reference impact. It identified seven main research streams: (1) Emerging Markets; (2) Sustainable Corporate Strategy; (3) Value Creation; (4) Branding Higher Education; (5) Financial Content Marketing; (6) Modernizing Healthcare; and (7). SME Development. From an empirical standpoint, the rolling out of content marketing enhances an organization's competitive advantage, resulting in a significant improvement in its social and economic standing.​
